key_insight: The paper introduces an ontology-grounded pipeline that automatically generates reasoner-verified multiple-choice benchmarks to evaluate whether LLMs can perform logically correct scientific reasoning.
engineering_relevance: This enables more reliable, scalable assessment of LLMs used in materials and biomedical AI, where incorrect reasoning can lead to unusable or unsafe outputs.
method: Generate MCQs from sufficiently axiomatised OWL 2 ontologies.
Create distractors by perturbing right-hand-side class expressions in class definition axioms.
Use OWL reasoner entailment checks to verify that incorrect answers are truly non-entailed.
evidence_signal: The authors generated 112, 2,491, and 15,216 MCQs from Pizza, PMDco, and DOID, and six zero-shot LLMs scored 41.1–76.8% accuracy versus a 25% random baseline.
watch_item: Benchmark quality depends on the ontology’s axiomatization and may be harder to generalize when source knowledge is sparse, inconsistent, or poorly modeled.
paper_title: Ontology-Grounded, Reasoner-Verified Benchmarks for Evaluating LLM Reasoning in Scientific AI
